gpt.rationale: If rent is unpaid when due, the landlord may terminate for nonpayment only if the tenant fails to pay within five days of the due date after the required statutory notice. federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)

elements_confirmed: The landlord failed to comply with the rental agreement or the statutory duty to maintain the dwelling unit in a fit and habitable condition as required by S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-440.
The tenant provided the landlord with written notice specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach.
The landlord was given a reasonable opportunity (at least 14 days) to remedy the breach after receipt of the notice.
The landlord failed to remedy the breach within the specified time.

The condition was not caused by the deliberate or negligent act or omission of the tenant, a member of his family, or other person on the premises with his permission or who is allowed access to the premises by the tenant.
